get.description: Which component version this deployment serves (versioning policy R4); the distribution manifest maps it to Distributions
Per-chain indexer health: live signal ages (facts) plus the staleness watchdog's stored verdicts. Staleness is data here, never an error status. Not an SLA.

verdicts_fresh.description: false = the watchdog itself is down or lagging (verdicts older than ~3 check intervals); `facts` remain authoritative, fall back to your own thresholds over them.

check_interval_minutes.description: Watchdog cadence; null when no verdicts exist yet.

status.description: Worst-of the two signal verdicts; `unmonitored` = chain has indexed data but no watchdog verdicts. Enum may grow values.

progress_age_seconds.description: Age of the newest indexing checkpoint touch. null = chain has nothing to index (idle, HEALTHY -- not unknown).

consumption_backlog_age_seconds.description: Age of the oldest confirmed-but-unconsumed log. null = empty backlog (HEALTHY).

evaluated_at.description: Unix seconds of the watchdog evaluation.

threshold_minutes.description: Watchdog threshold, minutes. Operational, may be retuned.
Watchdog threshold, minutes. Operational, may be retuned.

get.description: Every asset the registry holds. An asset has two NAMED source slots — a price source and a net-asset-value source — rather than a list; either may be null. `denomination` is carried on the source itself and returned verbatim.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size; values above 500 are clamped to 500.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Page start offset.

parameters.name: chain_id
parameters.description: The chain whose registry to read. Must be one of this deployment's served chains — see GET /registry/v1/registries. An unserved chain is a 400 `unknown-chain`.

address.description: The asset token's contract address, lowercased. The whole natural key.

name.description: The human-readable label recorded on the registry.

kind.description: Descriptive only — value derivation probes `asset()` live rather than trusting this.

price_source.description: The price source, or null when the asset has none. Price-mode oracles require one on every leg.

address.description: The aggregator (for AGGREGATOR_V3) or the tokenized vault (for ERC4626) this source reads from, lowercased.

source_type.description: What this source measures: a market price, or a net asset value.

source_interface.description: How this source is read: a Chainlink-style latestRoundData() feed, or a tokenized vault read through convertToAssets.

denomination.description: The registered denomination label this source quotes in, returned verbatim from the chain — it is carried on the source itself, so no extra lookup is involved. Resolve it to a unit address through GET /registry/v1/{chain_id}/denominations/{label}.

nav_source.description: The net-asset-value source, or null when the asset has none. In nav mode a leg without one falls back to its price source.

name.description: Live-read ERC-20 name; empty when the token omits it.

get.description: A feed is one edge in the graph the registry walks to prove an asset can reach US dollars: this base unit is priced in this quote unit, by this aggregator. `live` is read from the aggregator at the pinned block and is null when that call reverts; comparing `live.answer.decimals` to `feed_decimals` shows drift.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size; values above 500 are clamped to 500.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Page start offset.

parameters.name: chain_id
parameters.description: The chain whose registry to read. Must be one of this deployment's served chains — see GET /registry/v1/registries. An unserved chain is a 400 `unknown-chain`.

base.description: The unit the feed reports on: either a real token or a Chainlink pseudo-address such as 0x…0348 for US dollars. Lowercased.

quote.description: The unit the value is quoted in. Lowercased.

feed_decimals.description: The feed's decimals() as the registry recorded it at registration time.

live.description: Read from the aggregator at the pinned block; null when that call reverts.

raw.description: The integer exactly as the chain holds it, as a decimal string. Authoritative. A string because these values exceed the ~9.007e15 ceiling for exact integers in JSON numbers.

decimals.description: How many decimal places `raw` is scaled by. Always present.

formatted.description: `raw` shifted by `decimals`, as an exact decimal string. Lossless, and safe to display directly.

answer.description: The aggregator's latest answer. Its `decimals` is the aggregator's own CURRENT decimals(), which is not necessarily the `feed_decimals` the registry recorded — comparing the two shows drift.

updated_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC time of the aggregator's last update.

get.description: What joins the two halves of the registry together: an asset's source names a LABEL, a feed's endpoints are ADDRESSES. `label` is never null — the registry stores only the hash, so the text is read from the unit's own `symbol()`, with the two seed denominations (USD, ETH) coming from a fixed table because their units are code-less Chainlink pseudo-addresses. The symbol is taken at its word and NOT checked against `label_hash` — use `label_hash` as the identity. A unit that will not report a symbol returns 503.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size; values above 500 are clamped to 500.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Page start offset.

parameters.name: chain_id
parameters.description: The chain whose registry to read. Must be one of this deployment's served chains — see GET /registry/v1/registries. An unserved chain is a 400 `unknown-chain`.

label.description: The label as a display name, taken from the unit's symbol() and never null. On the list route this is not verified against label_hash — prefer label_hash as the identity.

label_hash.description: keccak256 of the label bytes — what the registry actually stores.

unit.description: The unit address this label names: a token, or a Chainlink pseudo-address such as 0x…0348 for US dollars. Lowercased.

get.description: A recipe is an approved CONTRACT ADDRESS implementing IMarketRecipe, not a record keyed by a mode string. Everything except `args` is read live from the recipe, so one registered after this service shipped still appears here and still describes itself — with args_known false. Note that getRecipes returns nothing until the owner Safe calls addRecipes, so an empty list is a correct answer, not a fault.

address.description: The recipe contract, lowercased. Its whole identity.

source.description: Which kind of rate this recipe works against, read from its own source(). `fixed` has no oracle mode — a fixed-rate market's oracle is keyed on a rate rather than on a pair.

formatted.description: `raw` shifted by `decimals`, as an exact decimal string. Lossless, and safe to display directly.

constants.description: The constants the recipe advertises, read live and keyed by their getter names. Scales differ per constant, which is why each carries its own `decimals`; the `_PERCENTAGE` constants are on the percentage scale, where 1e18 means one percent.

get.description: Get the rate oracle for a pair in one mode. Takes a MODE because one pair can hold a price wrapper and a net-asset-value wrapper simultaneously. PREDICTS when the oracle is not deployed, because on the limit-order path the adapter deploys it inside the fill — so at the moment a caller most wants the address, looking it up returns zero. Prediction simulates deploy rather than re-deriving the address off-chain, so it cannot drift from what the adapter will actually do.

parameters.description: The chain whose registry to read. Must be one of this deployment's served chains — see GET /registry/v1/registries. An unserved chain is a 400 `unknown-chain`.

mode.description: Which kind of rate oracle this is. One pair can hold both simultaneously, which is why the mode is part of the request.

status.description: `live` when the wrapper is already deployed; `predicted` when its address was derived by simulating deploy.

morpho_oracle.description: The Morpho oracle underneath the wrapper, read from its MORPHO_ORACLE() immutable. Available directly for a deployed wrapper. For a PREDICTED one there is no code to call, so it is only obtainable by chaining two calls inside one simulated block (eth_simulateV1); where the node cannot do that this is null rather than guessed.

post.description: Predict a market's oracle, pool id, and share tokens without deploying. Deploys nothing, signs nothing, and moves no funds. The rate constraint comes from a recipe contract, so the request takes a recipe address and its payload.
